claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among the quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary derivatives arise from composition-dependent local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion, quantified by DFT-calculated mean-square atomic displacement (MSAD), alters resistance to dislocation glide.
Alloys containing Cr have larger MSAD than the relevant non-Cr alloys.
Larger Cr-associated MSAD produces higher intrinsic strength, represented by extrapolated 0 K CRSS.
Higher proportions of Mn and Fe produce more pronounced dynamic solute pinning at elevated temperatures.
The quinary, listed quaternary, and listed ternary compositions can be treated as equiatomic FCC single crystals after the specified preparation.
Annealing for 168 h at 1273 or 1473 K followed by water quenching yields the stated homogenized initial condition.
Compression along [1̄23] can be used to determine the CRSS for (111)[1̄01] slip in these alloys.
At temperatures below room temperature, glide is primarily controlled by thermally activated overcoming of solid-solution obstacles.
Local lattice distortion creates an energy landscape that impedes dislocation glide.
At elevated temperatures, diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres elastically interact with moving dislocations.
The interaction of Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres with dislocations causes Portevin–Le Chatelier-type serrated flow.
The magnitude of Portevin–Le Chatelier strengthening scales with total Mn plus Fe content.
Relative to the quinary baseline, higher-Cr compositions should have higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS.
Relative to the quinary baseline, Mn/Fe-rich compositions should exhibit stronger serrated flow and a modest high-temperature CRSS increment.
CRSS should increase substantially as temperature decreases below room temperature because thermal activation is reduced.
The rate of CRSS increase on cooling should diminish below approximately 77 K because of dislocation-inertia effects.
Approximately 10% plastic strain corresponds to Stage I deformation and is suitable as the baseline for CRSS determination.

contradictions.description: The intervention covers 9–1373 K and the predictions discuss behavior below about 77 K and above 873 K, but the conditions and boundary exclude or ambiguously disclaim those inertia- and PL-dominated regimes. The boundary phrase stating validity 'below the inertial-dominated region (<60–77 K)' is also inconsistent with excluding temperatures below 60–77 K.

The conditions state that PL effects begin above 873 K, whereas the mechanism assigns PL behavior to 673–873 K and above. The baseline further describes 673–873 K as occurring before pronounced PL effects, leaving the onset range internally inconsistent.

The conditions describe CRSS determination at approximately 10% plastic strain, while the falsification experiment defines CRSS from the 0.2% offset yield stress. These are materially different operational definitions unless an explicit conversion or rationale is supplied.
